data.name: Mahfuz
data.gender_notes: Mahfuz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic verb 'hafaza', meaning 'to keep, to preserve, to protect'. In Islamic tradition, Mahfuz can refer to a person who is protected or guarded by Allah. The name Mahfuz carries the meaning “Preserved, Protected” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mahfuz usually hope their child will grow to embody preserved, protected and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for one who shields and guards the spiritual path of the individual
data.etymology: Mahfuz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Preserved, Protected.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahfuz total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Mahfuz
in_english.meaning: Forgiveness and pardon, one who is protected and preserved
in_english.long_meaning: Mahfuz is an Islamic name that means 'one who is protected and preserved' and has a rich etymology in Arabic. It is mentioned in the Quran as a name for those who are preserved and protected by Allah. The Arabic root of the name, 'h-f-z', conveys the idea of protection and preservation. In Islamic tradition, Mahfuz is associated with the concept of protection and preservation, highlighting the importance of safeguarding one's faith and integrity. The name is also linked to the idea of forgiveness and pardon, as it implies a state of being preserved and protected from sin and wrongdoing. Overall, Mahfuz is a name that reflects the values of protection, preservation, and forgiveness in Islam.
